lore.9001: Learned the craft from someone who is no longer around to be asked about it. Half the spells work, and so far the half that do not have been the more interesting ones.
lore.9002: Sells out rooms by losing badly on purpose, then wins the one nobody put money on. The knee is held together with tape and conviction.
lore.9003: Loads a spell into every chamber and has never once explained where the bullets go. The warrens turn out plenty of theorists; this one shoots.
lore.9004: A puddle with opinions. Whatever it was before it started imitating other things, it is honestly a little vague on the details itself.
lore.9005: Swore the oath in front of witnesses, which is the part that makes it binding. The armour was already secondhand when it was handed over.
lore.9006: Hears the sentence a moment before it is said, and has learned not to answer early. It is exhausting at parties.
lore.9007: Plays rooms that hold nine people and talks about them as though they held nine hundred. One of those numbers will be true eventually.
lore.9008: Works a small enchantment into everything that leaves the workshop, most of them harmless. The kettle has opinions now.
lore.9009: Calls things, and they come, which is only half the difficulty. Getting them to leave again is the part the books skip.
lore.9010: Left the order on good terms, or so the letter says, and still keeps the hours. The faith survived the paperwork better than the paperwork survived her.
lore.aleisterCrowley: Refounded the Mage Guild in the early 1900s with the backing of Britannia's royal house, styling it as a pseudo-chivalric order, hence the Sir and Lady titles its leaders still carry. As of 2001 he stands as one of the Guild's three pillars, representing the past, and has simply refused to ever step down; no one in the Guild can truly stand against him, since he knows spells even the gods do not.
lore.popePetrus: Born Joseph Ratzinger, he ascended to the Throne of Peter as Pietro II after John Paul II died from the assassination attempt of May 13, 1981. He has declared war on Jenna of Northpoint, refusing to recognize her as the Second Coming and branding her the Antichrist instead.
lore.draghi: His name is printed on tens of billions of banknotes and financial transaction logs, more times than the name of God across every printed Bible. The euro's security strip is laced with flecks of Fantablack scraped from the Omega Tower's outer walls, and between that arcane residue and the law that names are power, Draghi ascended as the godhead of the market itself, an abstract concept now driving the multiverse's economy from behind the scenes.
lore.billClinton: Current president of the Free States of Midwest, one of the three fragments the Americas were split into after independence never fully happened: the Republic of Cascadia on the east coast, the Free States of Midwest in the center, and the Atlantic Protectorate on the west coast under Britannia's control.
lore.margheritaHack: Head of the European Space Agency, currently testing new rockets built almost entirely from armor plating meant to be chewed apart by orbital debris, buying astronauts just enough time to clear low orbit. The Kessler Syndrome triggered during the Y2K event turned any ordinary launch into a coin flip with over 90% odds of failure.
lore.bubba: A mechanic from Westford, Texas, and something of a living legend. Built the Liminal Engine himself, a device that chews through dimensional energy and lets him drive across realities in a battered camper he calls The Beast. He once spent years running Route 666 with Eris, the goddess of discord, robbing banks by having her bend probability to crack any safe.
lore.selene: Made her money the way this branch of the Americas rewards: reading a market nobody else could hear and never once explaining the trick. She keeps a hitman's wardrobe and a broker's manners, and the two have never been in conflict, since both trades are about knowing exactly what a thing is worth to somebody else.
lore.andreotti: Seven times prime minister and never once caught, which he insists is the same as being innocent. Outlived every faction that meant to bury him by being the only person in the room who remembered what everyone in it had promised, and to whom, and on what day. Power wears out; paperwork does not.
lore.richardBenson: Broadcasts from a transmitter he built out of parts nobody will admit selling him, and has been at war with his own audience for twenty years. Fluent in three languages and hostile in all of them. Claims to have invented every genre he plays and to have been robbed of the credit for each one.
lore.ritaLeviMontalcini: Did the work that won her the Nobel in a bedroom laboratory, hiding from a state that had decided she was not permitted to be a scientist. Nothing since has been able to impress her, including the state, the Nobel, or her own century. Senator for life, and still the first one awake.
lore.kofiAnnan: Spent a career standing between people who had already decided to kill each other, and got enough of them to stop that the rest is a matter of arithmetic. Speaks quietly, on the theory that a room will lean in to hear a man who refuses to shout at it.
lore.georgeWBush: Inherited an oil fortune, a family name and a country in that order, and has been underestimated by everyone he has ever beaten. Runs on certainty rather than analysis, which is a liability in peacetime and something else entirely in a war.
lore.berlusconi: Owns the channels that report on him, which he has never regarded as a conflict so much as an efficiency. Sells optimism at scale and believes every word of it while he is saying it, which is what makes it sell.
lore.ciampi: Spent a lifetime holding the lira together and then signed it away for something steadier, and considers that the whole of his career rather than the end of it. Central bankers do not get statues; he has never once seemed to mind.

0: The branch behind her is a world where magic was never filed away among fairy tales but licensed, taxed and printed in the back pages of the newspapers.
Her dimension burned its last cathedral in 1913 and has run on borrowed miracles ever since.
The world she left was one flooded city ninety storeys tall, with the sea held back by recited law.
She grew up in a country that had quietly seceded from geography and could only be reached by getting lost on purpose.
In her reality the Y2K event never stopped, and it has been the first of January for eighteen months.
Her home branch is a Europe stitched together out of company towns, each one owned by a different sleeping god.
She arrives from a world where nobody died between 1971 and 1994, and everyone is still deciding whether that was a mercy.
The dimension behind her ran the Solomonic Ritual twelve times, industrially, and made a national holiday out of it.
Her reality never invented the wheel and never needed to, since distance there is a matter of persuasion.
She is from a timeline where the moon is a settled place and the night sky is crowded with lamps that answer to names.
1: There she was a licensed weather-witch, salting clouds for farming consortia.
She spent that life as a night nurse in a hospice for people whose deaths had gone missing.
She was the youngest archivist ever admitted to that world's Mage Guild, and the only one expelled from it twice.
In that life she was a courier, carrying sealed words between cities that refused to speak to each other.
She was a hedge-witch working out of a laundrette, doing curses at the going rate and never asking names.
There she was crowned, briefly, by a country that regretted it within the season.
She was that world's last practising exorcist, mostly employed by landlords.
She made her living reading the market by candlelight for men who called it research.
In that branch she taught primary-school arithmetic, and quietly held the town's bridge together with it.
She was a soldier there, in a war fought entirely by correspondence.
2: Then something in the sky opened a door that opened the wrong way, and she was on the far side of it.
It ended when she signed a contract she had not finished reading, and the ink outlived the world.
The end came as a sound, one long note, and everything that could hear it stopped being there.
She stepped into a lift going down and stepped out somewhere with a different number of directions.
A god she had never petitioned answered anyway, and the answer took the whole street with it.
She traded her dimension away in a wager she still insists she won.
The Liminal Engine of that world was switched on for testing, once, and she was standing too close.
Her name was written into someone else's ritual, and names are power, so she went where the name went.
Something enormous began remembering her, and the pressure of being remembered pushed her out.
She followed a stranger with her own face through a gap in a hedge, and the hedge closed.
3: She kept everything except the reason for any of it.
Ninety-two percent of her memories went into the payment; she does not know which ones, only that she flinches at church bells.
She lost her mother tongue in transit and has been borrowing this one ever since.
What she paid was her death, which now belongs to somebody else and is being kept badly.
She left with the clothes she stood in, a spear she cannot lift, and no proof she ever existed.
The crossing took her age; she is thirty-something and eleven at once, depending on the hour.
She surrendered every face she loved, and kept, uselessly, all of their birthdays.
Her shadow stayed behind, so she has learned to stand where nobody checks.
She gave up the last forty years of her own future and has not decided whether to miss them.
The toll was her talent, which grew back wrong, and much larger.
4: She turned up here on a road she does not remember choosing, and calls that a beginning.
Now she is on this branch, cataloguing the differences in a notebook she has already lost twice.
She has been here eleven days and is still testing which of her spells the local physics will tolerate.
She is looking for the version of this world where the door back is still standing open.
She says she is only passing through. She has said that in nine dimensions.
She has decided to treat this reality as a fresh sheet, and to stop counting.
She woke on Ritual Island with the tide out, alone, and started walking inland.
What she wants here is small and specific and she will not say what it is.
She is hunting whoever wrote her name into that ritual, across as many worlds as it takes.
For now she works for whoever pays, and asks the locals careful questions about their gods.

emRestlessLines: I am the protagonist. I am not being modest about it because I do not see the point of that.
I know a spell or two. I own four hundred grimoires and I have read most of them, so it is rather more than two.
This game is played better from my side of the net. You are welcome to the other side.
Choose me and I promise you hours of properly strange business. That is not a figure of speech. I have checked.
I am immortal across dimensions. Try to stop me. Genuinely, try, I want to see the attempt.
Witches never dies. ...somebody explained why that is wrong and I have decided to keep it.
Ninety-two percent of my memories were taken and I remain the strongest thing on this board. Consider what the other eight percent must be.
Still waiting. I have all the time there is, technically, and a very good backhand.
emOriginalLore: Born in Wimbledon, Britannia, in 1984, on the branch where the Ritual actually happened: this is dimension three, the original. She gave up ninety-two percent of her memories to forge the spear that killed the Father aspect of YHWH, and woke on Ritual Island with no past and a magical potential that has been growing past what she can hold ever since. Every other Em fell here from somewhere else; she never had anywhere to fall from.
emBackstory: Em was born in {town}, Britannia, and wanted to be a witch in an age that had filed magic away with the fairy tales.

When Margaret Thatcher, quietly one of the three pillars of the Mage Guild, needed a fulcrum for the Solomonic Ritual, she picked Em. Em offered herself as the sacrifice. The price was ninety-two percent of her memories.

They did not go anywhere. They were forged into the Lance of Memory, the spear that killed the Father aspect of YHWH: his soul was scattered into quadrillions of fragments, his rotting body still orbits the Earth, and every sacred spell the Vatican knew stopped working that night.

She did not die on the table. She woke alone on Ritual Island on the first of January with no past at all and, for reasons nobody has been able to explain, a magical potential grown enormously past what she started with. She is still learning to hold it, and it is still growing.

She travels with Bubba and the camper they share, pointed at Beagle for an appointment she barely remembers. Bubba feels nothing for her and still loves Eris; Eris, goddess of discord and current occupant of the celestial throne, is jealous enough to bend cosmic law and probability to make Em's life hell.

oldguard.name: The Old Guard
oldguard.desc: A knight, a cleric and a ranger who have worked the same roads for years and no longer need to agree out loud.

circle.name: The Arcane Circle
circle.desc: Three magicians who trained under the same roof and have been quietly competing ever since.

nightcrew.name: The Night Crew
nightcrew.desc: A thief, a mechanic and a gunmancer, put together for one job that never quite ended.

triage.name: The Triage Unit
triage.desc: Two people who keep the wounded alive and one who stands between them and whatever caused the wounds.

salvage.name: The Salvage Run
salvage.desc: A scientist, a technomage and a scout who sell whatever the orbit gives back.

convoy.name: The Convoy
convoy.desc: A mercenary, a tracker and a musician who have crossed more borders than any of them will admit to.

inquiry.name: The Quiet Inquiry
inquiry.desc: A journalist, a psyker and a necromancer, all asking the same question from three unsuitable directions.

kennel.name: The Kennel
kennel.desc: A tracker, a nurse and the shepherd dog that finds what neither of them can.

caravan.name: The Caravan
caravan.desc: A fortune teller, her driver and the goat that has outlived three of her predictions.
